item.title: What McDonald charges consumers for McRib amid lawsuit — a look at the chaotic history of the sandwich | Full details
item.description: McDonald’s faces a proposed class-action lawsuit alleging the McRib’s rib-shaped patty, marketing and premium price lead customers to expect pork rib meat. A judge allowed key claims to move forward, saying it was too early to accept the company’s argument. McDonald’s says the claims are inaccurate.
item.dc:creator: Garvit Bhirani
item.content:encoded: McDonald’s McRib sandwich is facing fresh scrutiny over its ingredients, price and distinctive rib-shaped appearance, with a proposed class-action lawsuit accusing the fast-food giant of misleading customers into believing they are paying for a premium pork-rib product. The legal challenge has gained momentum after a US federal judge declined to dismiss key claims in the case, allowing the dispute to proceed.The lawsuit has put the price of the limited-time sandwich under the spotlight. According to the complaint, the McRib cost reportedly as much as $7.89 before tax at some US outlets, making it one of the most expensive single-item options on McDonald’s menu when available. The plaintiffs said its premium pricing and limited availability reinforced the impression that it contained actual pork rib meat.A separate price comparison by Mashed found that one McDonald’s outlet was selling the sandwich for $5.99 this year, while a meal with fries and a drink cost $9.89. Prices, however, vary by restaurant and location. In 2010, the sandwich reportedly cost $2.69 on its own and $5.59 as a meal.Why is McDonald’s facing a lawsuit over McRib?Four consumers from California, New York, Illinois and Washington DC filed the proposed class-action lawsuit in December 2025, alleging that McDonald’s used the sandwich’s name, advertising and rib-shaped patty to create the impression that it contained pork rib meat.The complaint claims that the patty is made from restructured pork using lower-grade cuts, including shoulder, heart, tripe and stomach, rather than actual rib meat. The plaintiffs argued that customers would not have bought the sandwich, or would have paid less for it, had they known what it contained.The lawsuit described the use of the word “Rib” in the name and the patty’s shape as misleading. McDonald’s, however, has rejected the allegations, saying the sandwich is made with 100% pork sourced from farmers and suppliers across the US.In a statement according to AP, the company said the lawsuit “distorts the facts and many of the claims are inaccurate”. It also maintained: “We’ve always been transparent about our ingredients so guests can make the right choice for them.”What did the US court say?On October 30, US District Judge April Perry in Chicago rejected McDonald’s request to dismiss the proposed class action in its entirety, although some claims were dismissed.According to Reuters, the judge said it was premature to accept the company’s argument that reasonable consumers would not expect the McRib to contain rib meat. She also noted that customers should not be expected to research the ingredients of a fast-food sandwich before buying it.“Plaintiffs' proffered understanding of 'McRib' is not unreasonable or fanciful,” Perry wrote.The ruling does not establish that McDonald’s misled customers or that the sandwich contains the ingredients alleged in the complaint. The case will continue, with the plaintiffs seeking accountability over the product’s marketing.The chaotic history of McDonald’s McRibThe McRib has had an unusual journey since its debut in 1981. According to Business Insider, the sandwich was developed by McDonald’s chef René Arend as an alternative during a chicken shortage that left some restaurants struggling to meet demand for Chicken McNuggets.Made with boneless, restructured pork and shaped to resemble a rack of ribs, the sandwich was served with barbecue sauce, onions and pickles. Despite its launch, repeat sales were initially weak, and McDonald’s removed it from menus in 1985.Its subsequent returns helped turn it into one of the chain’s most recognisable limited-time offerings. The sandwich developed a dedicated following, with fans tracking its availability and campaigning for its return. It reportedly sold 30 million units in 2007, demonstrating the commercial appeal of bringing it back periodically.McDonald’s has also repeatedly promoted the sandwich’s departures as farewell events. The chain held a McRib “Farewell Tour” in 2005, followed by another in 2006. It returned nationwide in 2020 for the first time since 2012, before the company announced another farewell tour in 2022.That announcement did not mark the end of the sandwich. The McRib returned again in 2023, 2024 and 2025, with its recurring availability helping sustain interest among fans. In October 2026, McDonald’s brought it back from October 27 for a limited period at select US locations, including cities such as Los Angeles, Chicago, Miami and Dallas.McDonald’s CEO Chris Kempczinski has previously described it as “the GOAT of sandwiches on our menu”, using the popular acronym for “greatest of all time”. As per CBS News, during the 2022 farewell announcement, the company also left the door open for another return, saying, “Like any true farewell tour, we’re hoping this isn’t a 'goodbye' but a ‘see you later’."

MEXICO CITY, Oct 31 : Reserve driver Ryo Hirakawa will replace Esteban Ocon at Haas for this weekend's Mexico City Grand Prix, the US-owned Formula One team said on Saturday. • A team spokesman said the replacement was not due to illness but gave no further details. The governing FIA confirmed the change. • French driver Ocon is due to leave Haas at the end of the season, with Brazilian Rafael Camara moving up from Formula Two for 2027. • Japanese Hirakawa, 32, is a two-times world endurance champion and Le Mans 24 Hours winner with Toyota, who have a technical partnership with Ferrari-powered Haas. He took part in first practice at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez on Friday. • The race will be his Formula One debut and he partners Britain's Ollie Bearman in final practice and qualifying on Saturday before Sunday's race.

Source: Reuters

Oct 31 : Cryptocurrency exchange Binance said on Saturday it has been able to cover 90 per cent of the amount stolen after a record $6.3 billion hack of its platform. The outstanding 10 per cent consists of tokens that are less liquid, which means they may take longer to source in the required amounts, it said in a statement.  The exchange said it has set aside around $6.34 billion of company funds internally to cover the losses. Binance said the replenishment involved a partial deployment of its $1 billion Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), a bitcoin reserve it holds to protect customers in the event of security breaches.

The company's co-CEO, Richard Teng, said on Friday that the breach was a "complex attack" involving a compromised laptop and malicious software designed to delete evidence of its activity, making it harder to trace and investigate. Binance also said it had taken a new snapshot of assets held on its platform as of 0000 GMT on October 31, as part of its proof-of-reserves process. Users holding the 10 listed tokens — BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD, and ZEC — would be able to verify that their assets were backed at a minimum 1:1 ratio once the full proof was available, it said. The exchange said it remained on track to resume withdrawal services on Sunday, November 1, within its previously stated timeframe.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Binance says 90% of assets stolen in record hack have been replenished
item.description: Binance has replenished 90 per cent of the assets stolen in the October 29-30 cyberattack, which resulted in the loss of an estimated $6.3 billion to $6.4 billion in digital assets, news agency ...
item.dc:creator: Akshita Singh
item.content:encoded: Binance has replenished 90 per cent of the assets stolen in the October 29-30 cyberattack, which resulted in the loss of an estimated $6.3 billion to $6.4 billion in digital assets, news agency Reuters reported on Saturday.  The cryptocurrency exchange said the replenishment involved funds from its own corporate treasury, a portion of its Futures Insurance Fund and its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), Reuters said.  The exchange, as per the news agency, said its next priority was to resume withdrawal services for users. It also expects to partially deploy the SAFU fund over the next 24 hours as part of its replenishment efforts. The scale of the attack has raised concerns within the company, with employees privately expressing doubts about receiving their annual bonuses this year, even as Binance publicly maintained that it could easily reimburse the losses, people familiar with the matter said. The breach, which affected the exchange's hot wallets across 10 to 11 blockchains, including Ethereum, Bitcoin, Tron, Solana and the XRP Ledger, is being described as the largest cryptocurrency theft in history. The cryptocurrency industry has faced several major cyberattacks in recent years. Last month, exchange Bitget suffered an attack that resulted in the loss of $388 million. In February 2025, hackers stole nearly $1.5 billion from cryptocurrency exchange Bybit. However, the scale of the latest Binance breach has shocked even industry veterans.

LONDON, Oct 31 : Pressure intensified on beleaguered Manchester United manager Michael Carrick after his side finished with 10 men in a 2-0 Premier League defeat at Chelsea on Saturday to record their ninth straight game without a win in all competitions. The United board decided to stick with Carrick for the Chelsea game despite a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth last weekend after a 4-1 drubbing at Como in the Champions League but they lost again to goals from Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer. The result leaves United in provisional 16th spot with seven points from nine games, just a point above the relegation zone, while Chelsea are now in fourth place on 16 points. United, with captain Bruno Fernandes restored to the side after falling out with Carrick, looked lively in the first half but squandered a series of chances, notably from Fernandes, Matheus Cunha, who had a goal ruled offside, and Amad.

item.title: Solo tres monedas de América Latina superaron al dólar en octubre: cuáles ganaron y perdieron
item.description: Las divisas latinoamericanas mostraron resultados dispares durante octubre, ante la fortaleza del dólar, los movimientos de capital y las diferencias entre las políticas monetarias de la región.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Rodríguez Salcedo
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg Línea — Las monedas de América Latina cerraron octubre con resultados dispares frente al dólar. El peso colombiano ( USDCOP ) encabezó las ganancias, mientras que el real brasileño ( USDBRL ) y el peso mexicano ( USDMXN ) registraron las mayores pérdidas, en un mes marcado por las decisiones de la Reserva Federal. Ver más: Seis claves para entender por qué Intel se desploma casi 30% y Amazon cae tras sus resultados La fortaleza internacional del dólar, las expectativas sobre las tasas de interés en Estados Unidos y el encarecimiento del petróleo presionaron a varias divisas regionales. Sin embargo, los flujos de capital y las condiciones locales favorecieron a otras monedas. Los datos de Bloomberg muestran una apreciación de 3,58% del peso colombiano en el mes, frente a depreciaciones de 4,85% del real brasileño y 3,83% del peso mexicano. Julio Ruiz, economista en jefe de México de Citi, explicó que “el dólar tuvo un desempeño sólido durante octubre, apoyado por expectativas de una política monetaria estadounidense más restrictiva durante más tiempo y por un entorno de crecimiento relativamente favorable en comparación con otras economías avanzadas”. El peso colombiano destacó entre las monedas emergentes. Según Credicorp Capital, acumula una apreciación cercana al 18% en 2026, muy por encima del avance de aproximadamente 0,48% registrado por el real brasileño en el mismo periodo. Los analistas de Credicorp Capital atribuyeron parte de esa fortaleza al diferencial de tasas de interés de Colombia, la reducción de la prima de riesgo y la persistencia de operaciones de carry trade , que favorecieron la demanda extranjera de deuda soberana. La firma identificó además una paradoja en el comportamiento cambiario colombiano. Las dificultades fiscales del Gobierno incrementaron las expectativas de monetizaciones de recursos externos, un factor que contribuyó a presionar a la baja la cotización del dólar. → Suscríbete al newsletter Línea de Mercado , una selección de Bloomberg Línea con las noticias bursátiles más destacadas del día. Las estimaciones oficiales citadas por Credicorp apuntaban a monetizaciones de entre US$2.000 millones y US$3.000 millones durante el cierre de 2026, mientras que las proyecciones para 2027 se acercaban a US$15.000 millones. El repunte del petróleo también favoreció al peso colombiano, dada la condición de Colombia como exportador neto de crudo. El Brent volvió a dispararse durante octubre y llegó a superar los US$116 por barril, con efectos favorables sobre los términos de intercambio del país. El colón costarricense ( USDCRC ) ocupó el segundo lugar entre las monedas de mayor apreciación, con un avance de 0,63%, seguido del peso uruguayo, que ganó 0,30%, de acuerdo con las cifras de Bloomberg . Así se ha comportado el colón costarricense. Símbolo: CRC:CUR. Clase de activo: currency. En Costa Rica, el economista Daniel Zomer atribuyó la fortaleza del colón a cuatro fuentes de entrada de dólares: exportaciones, inversión extranjera directa, turismo y capitales financieros atraídos por las tasas de interés y la estabilidad política. Zomer describió el fenómeno como una situación en la que Costa Rica podría convertirse en víctima de su propio éxito. Según su análisis, las reservas internacionales se acercaban a US$20.000 millones, tras varios años de abundantes ingresos de divisas. El economista también señaló riesgos asociados con una eventual reversión de esos capitales financieros y con la pérdida de competitividad de algunos sectores exportadores, después de tres años y medio de apreciación cambiaria. Ver más: Alphabet registra su mayor caída en bolsa, mientras Microsoft limita sus pérdidas: 5 claves sobre la IA Por su parte, Patrizio Drago, Sales Trader de Adcap Uruguay, destacó el desempeño de la moneda uruguaya ( USDUYU ), que también mejoró su posición anual hasta el puesto 11 entre las 23 divisas emergentes seguidas por la firma. Drago señaló que el peso uruguayo acumulaba una depreciación cercana a 3% en 2026, ligeramente por debajo de la pérdida de 3,14% que registraba el sol peruano ( USDPEN ) en el mismo periodo. El especialista vinculó parte del comportamiento uruguayo con las expectativas de inversión extranjera, particularmente con el proyecto anunciado por la empresa española Solaria para desarrollar infraestructura de centros de datos. Así se ha comportado el sol peruano. Símbolo: USDPEN:CUR. Clase de activo: currency. “Esperábamos poder ofrecer un panorama más alentador a esta altura del año, pero el contexto internacional continúa marcado por la incertidumbre”, advirtió Drago. El real brasileño registró la mayor depreciación de América Latina durante octubre, con una caída de 4,85%, después de que las elecciones presidenciales provocaran fuertes movimientos en los mercados financieros. Davison Santana, analista de Bloomberg Intelligence , consideró que la recuperación de la demanda de operaciones de carry trade podría contribuir a estabilizar el real una vez se disipara el impacto electoral. Ver más: Cuatro escenarios para Wall Street y estrategias de inversión hasta junio de 2027, según UBS En su análisis, Santana sostuvo que “los mercados brasileños están preparados para seguir reconectándose con los factores globales a medida que se desvanece el impacto poselectoral”. El analista señaló que los participantes del mercado ya reportaban nuevas entradas de dólares y que una ruptura del nivel de BRL$5,31 por dólar abriría espacio para una recuperación hacia BRL$5,25. Sin embargo, el deterioro de las perspectivas fiscales continuaba como uno de los principales riesgos para Brasil. Las promesas electorales y las dificultades presupuestarias podían mantener elevada la prima exigida por los inversionistas. Así se ha comportado el real brasileño. Símbolo: USDBRL:CUR. Clase de activo: currency. El peso mexicano registró la segunda mayor depreciación de la región, con una caída de 3,95%. La moneda sufrió el efecto combinado del fortalecimiento internacional del dólar y las expectativas sobre las políticas monetarias de Estados Unidos y México. Ruiz, de Citi, explicó que “la combinación de un dólar más fuerte a nivel global, una Reserva Federal percibida como más hawkish y el repunte de las expectativas de tasas en EE.UU. redujo el atractivo relativo de las monedas emergentes de alto carry , entre ellas el peso”. La posibilidad de futuros recortes de tasas del Banco de México también redujo el atractivo relativo de la moneda. A ello se sumaron, según Ruiz, las preocupaciones sobre la consolidación fiscal y la prima de riesgo de los activos mexicanos. Ver más: El desplome de la bolsa de Brasil por Lula deja un contagio limitado en América Latina El peso chileno ( USDCLP ) también estuvo bajo presión, con una depreciación de 1,89%. Emanoelle Santos, analista de mercados de XTB, relacionó su caída con el repunte del petróleo, la fortaleza del dólar y las expectativas de tasas estadounidenses elevadas durante más tiempo. Santos explicó que “el cobre, en cambio, ha actuado más bien como un amortiguador de la caída del peso, ya que se ha mantenido alrededor de US$6,5 a US$6,7 la libra y la demanda física china sigue mostrando señales de fortaleza”. La especialista señaló que la economía china creció 4,5% en el tercer trimestre, mientras que la inversión fija retrocedió 7,2% en los primeros nueve meses. Esa combinación limitó el respaldo que los altos precios del cobre podían ofrecer al peso chileno. Así se ha comportado el peso chileno. Símbolo: USDCLP:CUR. Clase de activo: currency. El Banco Central de Chile mantuvo su tasa de política monetaria en 4,5%, pero esa decisión resultó insuficiente para contrarrestar las presiones externas, de acuerdo con Santos. Otras monedas también perdieron terreno durante octubre. El guaraní paraguayo ( USDPYG ) retrocedió 1,44%, el peso dominicano ( USDDOP ) cayó 1,26%, el peso argentino ( USDARS ) cedió 1,07% y el sol peruano ( USDPEN ) se depreció 1,05%. En Perú, Milagros Cruzado, analista de mercados de Capitaria, señaló que el tipo de cambio pasó de aproximadamente S/3,36 a niveles de entre S/3,43 y S/3,45 durante las últimas semanas. Ver más: ¿Qué pasa con las bolsas, los bonos y el dólar cuando la Fed sube las tasas de interés? Cruzado explicó que “aunque el sol se depreció en ese periodo, el movimiento no se ha convertido en una tendencia sostenida: se trata más de un ajuste puntual frente a un entorno externo más exigente que de un deterioro de los fundamentos peruanos”. La especialista destacó que las reservas internacionales cercanas a US$96.000 millones y los ingresos por exportaciones de cobre continuaban como soportes de la moneda, aunque el petróleo más caro aumentó la demanda de dólares de los importadores. En Argentina, Federico Filippini, Head of Research & Strategy de Adcap, señaló que el dólar se depreció durante octubre, aunque el comportamiento cambió en la última semana por las presiones regionales y la demanda de cobertura. Filippini destacó que el Banco Central argentino compró más de US$1.200 millones durante el mes y que las reservas brutas superaron los US$50.600 millones, frente a US$46.090 millones al cierre de septiembre. El especialista advirtió que la debilidad de la actividad económica y las expectativas relacionadas con las elecciones de 2027 podrían anticipar una mayor dolarización de carteras, pese al respaldo de la balanza comercial y la oferta estacional de divisas. Entre las monedas con menores variaciones, el quetzal guatemalteco y la lempira hondureña registraron depreciaciones de 0,11% cada una, según los datos de Bloomberg . Ver más: Oro digital: cómo funcionan Tether Gold y Paxos Gold, los principales tokens respaldados por oro Las perspectivas para el cierre de 2026 dependerán principalmente de las decisiones de la Reserva Federal, la evolución del dólar internacional y los precios de las materias primas, aunque los factores políticos y fiscales mantendrán un peso importante en algunos países. Ruiz, de Citi, sostuvo que “hacia el cierre del año seguimos viendo sesgos favorables para el dólar, aunque probablemente más moderados que los observados recientemente”. El economista identificó como principal riesgo una moderación de las expectativas sobre la Fed o señales más visibles de desaceleración económica en Estados Unidos. Para México, el economista identificó como factores relevantes una postura menos favorable a los recortes de Banxico y posibles avances en las negociaciones comerciales con Estados Unidos. En Chile, Santos señaló que una moderación de la inflación estadounidense y del petróleo, acompañada de precios elevados del cobre y señales de estabilización económica en China, podría favorecer una recuperación del peso. Ver más: ¿Vale la pena comprar bonos latinoamericanos? Morgan Stanley señala cuatro mercados con primas atractivas Para Perú, Cruzado destacó que “en diciembre, el pago de gratificaciones suele aumentar la demanda de soles, lo que podría darle un soporte estacional a la moneda, aunque ese efecto no está garantizado”. El cobre y las decisiones de la Fed también serán determinantes para el tipo de cambio. En Colombia, Credicorp Capital anticipó la posibilidad de una corrección ordenada de la reciente fortaleza del peso, mientras que en Brasil los inversionistas seguirán atentos al comportamiento de los flujos extranjeros y a las cuentas fiscales.

Go To Pakistan

Shehbaz Sharif celebrates Pakistan’s Hong Kong Sixes win over India. Pakistanis are embarrassed

Pakistan chased down India’s 88-run total in less than four overs, but some Pakistanis questioned the prime minister’s exuberant response.

Debdutta Chakraborty

31 October, 2026 07:30 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

File photo of Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif | Photo: Reuters

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

Pakistan beat India on Friday in the Hong Kong Sixes, a six-over match played between teams of six players. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, however, treated the rare win as a major achievement, drawing ridicule even from some Pakistanis.

The Hong Kong Sixes is a six-a-side tournament in which matches are played over six overs per innings. Batting first, India managed just 88 for five, the lowest total of the day. Pakistan chased down the target in less than four overs.

Sharif congratulated the team on X, also praising the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB).

Show Full Article

“Congratulations to our boys on a superb four-wicket victory over India in the opening clash of the Hong Kong Sixes 2026!” he wrote. He also commended PCB chairman Mohsin Naqvi and his team for their efforts in preparing and supporting the players.

The congratulatory message, however, drew amusement and criticism from some Pakistani users. An X user, Lahori Guy, pointed to Pakistan’s recent record against India in major international competitions, writing: “Pak got humiliated in last 5 yrs in every ICC match Vs Ind and you are celebrating HK Sixes Win that has no value.”

Another user simply asked: “What is wrong with this Cartoon??”

X user Saad described Sharif as an “international embarrassment”.

Indians, too, joined in. Former cricketer Ajay Jadeja responded to Sharif’s post, saying: “Congratulations on winning the Hong Kong Sixes World Cup match against India. Now, it’s time for the Victory Parade”

The win offered Pakistan a much-needed boost after the team had been on the brink of elimination following a one-wicket defeat to the UAE in its opening match earlier in the day.

The three-day tournament will see group winners advance to the semi-finals, with the final scheduled to take place at the Mission Road Ground in Mong Kok on 1 November.

What is the Hong Kong Sixes? First held in 1993, the Hong Kong Sixes was designed to allow local players and fans to watch leading international cricketers compete. The tournament features national teams and has attracted established players over the years, although its format is markedly different from traditional cricket.

Matches are played between six-a-side teams, with six overs per innings, making for shorter contests and more aggressive batting. The tournament ran regularly through much of the 1990s and 2000s before its schedule was disrupted by the growth of franchise-based T20 leagues. It returned in 2024.

India and Pakistan have a history in the competition. The two sides met in last year’s edition, when India beat Pakistan by two runs.

This year, however, Pakistan came out on top with a four-wicket victory.

(Edited By Raunaq Lekhi)

item.title: China pierde impulso económico en octubre ante contracción de la actividad industrial
item.description: El PMI manufacturero cayó a 49,3 en octubre, por debajo de las previsiones del mercado y del umbral que marca la expansión. La debilidad aumenta la presión sobre Pekín para impulsar la segunda mayor e ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — La actividad industrial de China se ralentizó en octubre, lo que pone de relieve los retos a los que se enfrentan los responsables políticos en su intento por mantener la recuperación económica y garantizar que se alcance el objetivo de crecimiento de este año. El índice oficial de gestores de compras del sector manufacturero descendió hasta 49,3 desde el 50,1 registrado en septiembre, según informó el sábado la Oficina Nacional de Estadística. Este dato contrasta con la previsión media de 49,9 obtenida en una encuesta de Bloomberg a economistas. Una lectura superior a 50 indica expansión. Ver más: Marcas chinas superan a las japonesas en ventas de autos en Europa por primera vez El índice de actividad no manufacturera, que abarca la construcción y los servicios, se situó en 49,7, frente al 50,2 registrado en septiembre. Este deterioro sugiere que la segunda economía más grande del mundo ha perdido algo de impulso al inicio del cuarto trimestre, tras un modesto repunte en los tres meses anteriores. Pekín podría verse sometida a una mayor presión para ofrecer apoyo adicional tras haber introducido un nuevo paquete de medidas de estímulo específicas en las últimas semanas, ya que los responsables políticos tratan de mantener el crecimiento en la senda adecuada para cumplir el objetivo anual del gobierno, situado entre el 4,5% y el 5%. La debilidad se extendió tanto a la oferta como a la demanda: el índice de producción manufacturera cayó 1,9 puntos porcentuales hasta situarse en 49,8 y el indicador de nuevos pedidos descendió 1,1 puntos porcentuales hasta situarse en 49,4, según la oficina de estadística. Las grandes empresas manufactureras se mantuvieron en fase de expansión, con un índice de 50,2, mientras que los índices correspondientes a las medianas y pequeñas empresas descendieron hasta 48,4 y 47,5, respectivamente. El PMI del sector manufacturero de alta tecnología se situó en 51,3, registrando una expansión incluso cuando la actividad industrial global se contrajo. Ver más: “El financiamiento de China se ha replegado en el mundo”: estos son los desafíos para sus deudores en América Latina El gobierno ya ha intensificado las políticas destinadas a impulsar la economía, ofreciendo más apoyo crediticio a las pequeñas empresas y a los consumidores, subvenciones hipotecarias para algunos compradores de vivienda y cuotas adicionales de emisión de bonos para las administraciones locales. También se han puesto en marcha las obras de grandes proyectos de infraestructura, como el de las “Seis Redes”, y las autoridades han manifestado su disposición a introducir nuevas medidas si fuera necesario. -Con la c olaboración de Tian Ying. item.title: ¿Dónde es más caro vivir en América Latina?: estas son las ciudades que lideran el Índice de Costo de Vida en 2026¿Dónde es más caro vivir en América Latina?: estas ...
item.description: América Latina está sufriendo nuevas presiones inflacionarias en un contexto de mayores precios de la energía y los alimentos.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Salazar Castellanos
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg Línea — La capital de Costa Rica, un país con uno de los salarios mínimos más altos de la región en dólares y con mayor calidad de vida, es el lugar más costoso para vivir en América Latina en 2026, según datos del ‘ Cost of Living Index’ de la plataforma Numbeo. San José tiene un índice de costo de vida del 59,2, el más alto entre los países de América Latina y el Caribe incluidos en el listado, de acuerdo con los datos más actualizados de la base de datos en línea. Ver más: Los 5 países de América Latina con mayor calidad de vida en 2026, según clasificación de Wharton El alto costo de vida en Costa Rica se explica por salarios y cargas sociales elevados, mayores costos de energía y logística, un mercado pequeño que limita las economías de escala y una menor competencia en algunos sectores. A esto se suman los precios de la vivienda y los servicios, impulsados por la inversión extranjera y la concentración económica. Montevideo es la segunda ciudad más cara en la región, con un índice de 50,8, seguida por Kingston (Jamaica) con 57,7; Puerto Vallarta (México) con 52,8 y Buenos Aires (Argentina), con 52,4. Ver más : ¿Qué tan cara o barata está tu moneda frente al dólar? Esto revela el Índice Big Mac para América Latina Más abajo están San Miguel de Allende (México) con 52,3; Monterrey (México) con 50,8; Ciudad de Panamá con 49,1; Cancún (México) con 49; y Ciudad de México con 48,9. En el top 10 del ‘ Cost of Living Index’ , México es el país con mayor contribución en el listado con cinco ciudades. Este índice compara cuánto cuestan los bienes y servicios básicos —como comida, transporte, restaurantes y servicios públicos— en distintas ciudades del mundo, aunque no toma en cuenta el costo de la vivienda. Por ejemplo, si una ciudad tiene un índice de 120, significa que vivir allí es un 20% más caro que en Nueva York en términos de gastos diarios, sin contar el arriendo o la hipoteca. “Lo que encarece a San José, Montevideo, Buenos Aires o Puerto Vallarta es que llega gente con dólares a buscar dónde vivir. Son ciudades con vida cultural, vuelos directos a Estados Unidos y Europa, buen internet y trámites de residencia relativamente sencillos”, dijo a Bloomberg Línea el analista Cristian Gutiérrez. “Para mí la vivienda es lo que define si una ciudad es cara o barata, porque es por ahí que entra la demanda de afuera. La comida sigue siendo lo que más golpea a las familias de menos ingresos, y los servicios se disparan cuando quitan subsidios”. Ver más: Cepal rebaja su previsión de crecimiento para América Latina en 2026: así quedan las proyecciones por país Fuente: Numbeo Entre los factores que encarecen el costo de vida en varias de las ciudades que encabezan la tabla está el tamaño reducido de sus economías y su alta dependencia de las importaciones. Estas ciudades están en países con mercados internos reducidos y poca producción local de bienes de consumo, lo que obliga a importar muchos productos, lo que encarece precios por aranceles, transporte y tipo de cambio, ha explicado a Bloomberg Línea en Colombia la doctora en Economía y profesora de la Universidad del Rosario, Clara Inés Pardo. También influye en la balanza el hecho de tener monedas relativamente fuertes o dolarizadas, los altos impuestos y cargas laborales, los servicios públicos y privados costosos, así como el efecto del turismo y la inversión extranjera que encarece ciertos sectores. Entre tanto, ciudades consideradas como más baratas combinan economías más grandes o con mayor producción local, salarios promedio más bajos, vivienda más asequible y menor presión tributaria sobre consumo. “Santa Cruz, Recife, Salvador, Fortaleza, Cuenca o Asunción son baratas por lo que les falta. Tienen pocos vuelos internacionales directos, están poco conectadas con los mercados globales y casi no llegan extranjeros a comprar o arrendar”, consideró el analista Gutiérrez. También hay un factor a tener en cuenta en relación a la informalidad. Fuente: Numbeo Al respecto, la analista Clara Inés Pardo dice que una economía informal grande reduce los costos de vida, ya que muchas actividades (comercio, servicios o transporte) funcionan fuera del sistema tributario formal, abaratando costos. Otro factor es el acceso a transporte y servicios públicos a precios bajos o subsidiados, lo que reduce los gastos diarios. Pardo ha explicado a este medio que el ingreso no tiene el mismo poder económico ni cumple la misma función en todos los países. “El umbral de bienestar está condicionado por el costo de vida, el poder adquisitivo, las condiciones materiales y las expectativas de consumo de cada sociedad”. Según la Comisión Económica para América Latina y el Caribe (Cepal), la región está sufriendo nuevas presiones inflacionarias en un contexto de mayores precios de la energía y los alimentos. Explicó que estas presiones repercuten en los costos de producción y transporte, y afectan especialmente a los hogares que destinan una mayor proporción de sus ingresos a bienes esenciales. “Las presiones inflacionarias y mayores tasas de interés globales podrían reducir el margen para flexibilizar la política monetaria en las economías de la región”, indicó la Cepal. Ver más: Mapa de los países de ingresos más altos y bajos en Latinoamérica, según el Banco Mundial

LONDON, Oct 31 : Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes was restored to the starting lineup against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday by under-pressure manager Michael Carrick after he dropped the Portuguese international last weekend. United lost 3-0 at home to Bournemouth in the Premier league on Sunday without Fernandes, who was dropped after criticising tactics following a 4-1 drubbing at Como in the Champions League. United sit one point above the relegation zone after a string of poor results this season under their former midfield stalwart Carrick. Chelsea are also looking for a morale-boosting result after losing 2-0 at home to London rivals Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League last weekend and against Liverpool in the League Cup fourth round on penalties on Wednesday. Manager Xabi Alonso picked 19-year-old Estevao to start following criticism from fans that the exciting Brazil winger was underused and amid media talk he could be looking to move.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Nevada Governor's Race Is Democrats’ Working-Class Test for 2028
item.description: President Donald Trump built his political career on being a working-class whisperer, winning over not only most White voters without four-year college degrees, but significant numbers of blue-collar Latino and Black voters as well. While polls indicate Trump’s Republicans don’t stand a chance of replicating his success in the midterms, this hasn’t quieted the debate among Democrats over how best to out-whisper the whisperer.
item.dc:creator: Erika D. Smith

item.title: Patrick Stewart Embodied the Value of Aging Actors in Hollywood
item.description: For generations of fans, prolific actor Patrick Stewart had become inseparable from the characters he played. So when news came that he died on Wednesday, many paid tribute to the 86-year-old by invoking the fictional icons he left behind.
item.dc:creator: Miles Surrey

item.title: Halloween Candy Has Taken the Free Spirit Out of Kids’ Holiday
item.description: We’re better off without the mayhem the day was once known for. But have we traded the lessons of freedom for cheap sugar?
item.dc:creator: Brooke Sample

item.title: Cost of Living Looms Over the Midterms
item.description: Bloomberg Economics Economic Statecraft Lead Chris Kennedy tells Bloomberg This Weekend that higher costs for gasoline, groceries and housing are weighing on voters and putting pressure on parts of the coalition Donald Trump assembled in 2024. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Kennedy explains how affordability concerns are playing out in states including Michigan, Iowa and Texas and how control of Congress could shape economic policy after the midterms. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ukraine Strikes Bashneft Refineries as Russia Attacks Power Grid
item.description: Ukraine’s drone forces struck a complex of refineries deep within Russia, even as Kyiv and other parts of the country struggled to restore electricity following overnight Russian strikes on energy infrastructure.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Iran Threatens Wider US Strikes Even as Talks Make Progress
item.description: Iran’s Supreme Leader ordered his top military commanders to prepare for renewed confrontation with the US and Israel and expand Tehran’s options for retaliation, even as his top diplomat signaled progress in diplomatic talks.

item.title: AI Spending Fears Hammer Big Tech Stocks
item.description: Bloomberg Senior Editor for Technology and Strategic Industries Mike Shepard tells Bloomberg This Weekend that disappointing Big Tech earnings are intensifying investor concerns about whether massive AI spending will generate sufficient returns, as Alphabet and Intel come under particular pressure. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Lisa Mateo, Shepard also discusses the record $6.3 billion Binance hack and the possibility that North Korean hackers were responsible. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.dc:creator: TBS NEWS DIG
item.content:encoded:
中間選挙でトランプ大統領に“逆風”　高まる「反イスラエル感情」　揺らぐユダヤ系アメリカ人の影響力【報道特集】

TBSテレビ

2026年10月31日(土) 20:30

国際 報道特集

トランプ大統領の判断に影響与えるイスラエル　蜜月の歴史

10月22日～26日にロイター通信が行った世論調査によると、「きょう選挙が行われるとしたらどちらの党の候補に投票するか」との質問に、47％が民主党と答え、共和党と答えたのは36％だった。

共和党への支持が伸び悩む背景にあると考えられているのが、トランプ大統領が進めたイランへの軍事攻撃を機に急速に進んだ物価高だ。

しかし、トランプ大統領は強硬姿勢を崩さない。

トランプ大統領

「短期的には影響が出るが、大したことはない。狂ったイランから核兵器を取り上げるには安いくらいだ」

トランプ大統領の判断に影響を与えているのが、ともにイランへの軍事攻撃に踏み切ったイスラエルだ。

27日、総選挙が行われたイスラエルの街中にも、ネタニヤフ首相とトランプ大統領を描いた広告が掲げられていた。

1948年、「ユダヤ教徒の悲願」として建国されたイスラエルに対し、アメリカは絶えず支援を行ってきた。その関係の深さを物語る場所がニューヨークにある。

村瀬キャスター

「ニューヨークの中でも特にユダヤ人の多い地域です。この街を見ると、ヘブライ語の看板も並んでいます。アメリカの中にあって、まるでこの地域だけがイスラエルにいるような雰囲気も漂う街になっています」

この地区では、第二次世界大戦中のヨーロッパでの迫害を逃れてきたユダヤ人らが、独自のコミュニティを作って暮らしてきた。

――まもなく中間選挙ですね。投票する予定ですか？

ユダヤ系アメリカ人

「私は大の共和党支持者です。トランプの大ファンです。次の救世主・メシアだと信じています。トランプほど、イスラエルに尽くしてくれた人が過去にいたでしょうか」

ユダヤ系アメリカ人

「誰に投票するかは言えませんが、この地区の住民ならユダヤ系アメリカ人の保護に最も適した人物を支持するでしょう。反ユダヤ主義と闘い、イスラエルの地を守ってくれる人物です。神を信じていれば心配ありません。神が私たちを守ってくれます」

US campaign for control of Congress enters final weekend

Voters arrive to vote in the congressional midterm election at a polling station at Midtown Mall in Anchorage, Alaska, US, on Oct 30, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Emily Mesner)

FAST

WASHINGTON: As the campaign for control of the US Congress reached its final weekend, the Trump administration stepped up its legal intervention in the Alaska Senate race while the number of Americans casting early ballots neared 50 million, a record for a midterm election. The Department of J us tice accelerated its criminal investigation in Alaska on Friday (Oct 30), following reports that aides to a Democratic Senate candidate recruited a retired schoolteacher from a remote fishing village to get on the ballot beca us e he has the same name as the Republican incumbent. The DOJ, acting on a civil lawsuit that US President Donald Trump said he instigated, also filed further motions in an attempt to block the state of Alaska from certifying the Senate results if the Republican incumbent, Dan S. Sullivan, loses a close race on a ballot that includes the nonpartisan candidate Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. The closely contested race in Alaska is seen as crucial for the Democrats if they hope to take control of the Senate from Trump's Republicans in Tuesday's vote. PROSECUTOR ALLEGES "SHAM CANDIDATE" IN KEY ALASKA RACE

It is one of 35 races in the 100-member Senate that will set the tone for Trump's final two years in office. Also up for grabs are all 435 seats in the US Ho us e of Representatives. Early voter participation this cycle has set a record. More than 49 million Americans have already cast ballots, either in person or by mail, according to the University of Florida's Election Lab, up from nearly 46 million who voted before Election Day in the last midterms, in 2022. A Democratic victory in one or both chambers could result in congressional investigations of the Trump administration, which for two years has enjoyed largely compliant Republican majorities. Trump has been on a campaign blitz in multiple states over the past month but is not scheduled to travel on Saturday, when there will be a mash-up of American traditions: politics, Halloween and college football across the country. Trump returns to the campaign trail on Sunday in Kansas and Iowa. The DOJ's top prosecutor in Alaska, US Attorney Michael Heyman, said at a Friday press conference that a recent New York Times article about the supposed recruitment effort had driven a "surge" of FBI resources, adding that he had assigned several prosecutors to the case and that investigative steps were taking place "intensely and swiftly". The Times reported on Wednesday that aides to Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola recruited Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. to run. Heyman labelled him a "sham candidate" but declined to say what crime may have been committed. The department had already filed its civil action but, Heyman said, "when the New York Times article hit, that's additional information that accelerated what we've been doing". Peltola has denied knowing about any effort to recruit the second Sullivan. The retired teacher has denied coordinating with Peltola's campaign .

Related:

Trump cancels weekend rallies, plans to phone in to other midterm campaign events

Beyond Trump: US midterms offer early test in battle for White House in 2028

ADMINISTRATION GETS INVOLVED IN RACES NATIONWIDE The Trump administration has also sued California to try to prevent the counting of ballots cast by more than 20,000 registered voters who the administration alleged could be noncitizens. It has also sued roughly 30 states and the District of Columbia, seeking unredacted voter rolls, part of a pattern that has alarmed election officials. A federal judge on Friday ordered the DOJ to stop threatening to prosecute California election officials who do not comply with the Trump administration's directives regarding alleged voting by noncitizens. Sean Morales-Doyle, director of the voting rights and elections program at the Brennan Center for J us tice, said the administration’s actions parallel the tactics undertaken by election deniers in the 2020 presidential election. While the administration is unlikely to win in court, he said, the efforts could create a political atmosphere that leads to official misconduct. “It's about creating uncertainty, sowing fear, distr us t, chaos, hoping that you create the political circumstances in which maybe the lieutenant governor of Alaska does feel pressure to do something that they're not supposed to do. Maybe the governor does start to question things, too,” Morales-Doyle said. Even so, a bipartisan majority of US voters tr us t the overall electoral process, with 76 per cent saying they are confident their ballots will be counted accurately, according to a Sep 30 to Oct 5 Reuters/Ipsos poll. Some 15 per cent were not confident and the rest were not sure or did not answer the question. Confidence was about equally high among Republicans and Democrats.

Source: Reuters/co

item.title: Los 10 dulces más populares de Halloween 2026: el dulce negocio de US$4.100 millones
item.description: No hay Halloween sin una buena dosis de dulces y este año chocolates, gomitas y caramelos masticables competirán por conquistar el paladar (y el bolsillo) de los consumidores en una temporada clave ...
item.dc:creator: Isaac Garrido
item.content:encoded: No hay Halloween sin una buena dosis de dulces y este año chocolates, gomitas y caramelos masticables competirán por conquistar el paladar (y el bolsillo) de los consumidores en una temporada clave para la industria de la confitería. Según la Federación Nacional de Minoristas de Estados Unidos (NRF, por sus siglas en inglés), los estadounidenses gastarán US$4.100 millones en dulces. ¿Pero qué golosinas desbordarán por las cubetas de los niños que recorren las calles pidiendo truco o trato? Como cada año, CandyStore.com, una tienda especializada en la comercialización de dulces al mayoreo, presentó su ranking anual donde los famosos chocolates M&M’s se colocaron como el dulce más popular de la temporada. La clasificación se basa en el peso de los dulces vendidos y a partir de ahí se hacen proyecciones por estado y nacionales. Luego de los tradicionales chocolates de la compañía Mars, las gomitas ácidas Sour Patch Kids se colocaron en el segundo puesto. El movimiento no es inusual, pues la periodista de gastronomía del New York Times Kim Severson explicó que la generación Z está impulsando los sabores ácidos y frutales a través de retos en redes sociales. Una prueba de ello es que los Skittles, los coloridos caramelos suaves masticables con sabores a frutas, llegaron a la tercera posición. En la cuarta posición se ubican los Reese’s Cup, chocolates en forma de canastilla rellenos de crema de cacahuate, que durante la temporada suelen llegar en ediciones limitadas en forma de calabaza. La Asociación Nacional de Confiteros de Estados Unidos señaló que el 89% de los consumidores disfruta de los productos de temporada con sabores, formas o empaques especiales. Detrás de ellos, el ranking ubicó los NERDS Gummy Clusters, unas gomitas cubiertas con los ácidos caramelos caracterizados por una cobertura crujiente. Severson destacó que para Halloween 2026 dos tercios de los hogares en EE.UU. prevén comprar golosinas, que han registrado incrementos del 71% desde 2021.

Harmer, Rabada steer South Africa to series win over Australia

FAST

CAPE TOWN, Oct 31 : South Africa spinner Simon Harmer took a career-best 6-16 and Kagiso Rabada became the fastest by balls bowled to reach 350 test wickets as the hosts thumped Australia by 176 runs to clinch their three-match series 2-1 at Newlands on Saturday. Set a target of 288 for victory, the tourists were bowled out for 111 as South Africa leapfrogged them to go top of the test world rankings for the first time since January 2016. Australia had hopes of chasing down the total but lost two wickets in the first over of the final day and slumped to 62 for eight as their effort became a battle of survival that South Africa ended before tea. There will be questions asked of this Australia side in the wake of the defeat, not least another poor batting display and the decision to bowl on the opening morning that left them batting last on a wearing wicket.

"The trend of this game was once you got yourself in there were runs to be had," Australia captain Pat Cummins said. "But within the first hour the game was away from us and we did not give ourselves a chance. "We are a really good side but playing tough opponents away from home is always difficult. We came here thinking we were good enough to win but we couldn't do it." Hopes of victory evaporated in the first half hour as Rabada (3-39) removed the top three batters to take his tally to 350 test wickets, taking 13,808 deliveries, fewer than compatriot Dale Steyn (14,719) and Pakistan’s Waqar Younis (14,905). After that Harmer came into his own, exploiting the conditions expertly to also claim a first 10-wicket haul in tests with figures of 10-120 across the match.   Rabada removed opener Matt Renshaw (0), caught by wicketkeeper Ryan Rickelton down the leg side, and the struggling Marnus Labuschagne (4) leg before wicket in the first over of the innings He then had the dangerous Travis Head caught at gully by Marco Jansen to rock Australia early on. First-innings centurion Josh Inglis (4) was run out attempting a quick single to compound Australia’s woes, and from there Harmer took the last six wickets. Cummins (11 from 90 balls) and innings top-scorer Nathan Lyon (33 not out) delayed the inevitable with a ninth-wicket stand that lasted 17.2 overs, but Harmer trapped the former lbw and then bowled Josh Hazlewood to seal the win. "It was just understanding what I needed to do, getting the ball in the right areas as often as I could, and playing with my pace and trajectories, the little nuances I have learnt along the way. It all worked out alright," Harmer said. "Today was a lot of fun, fielders around the bat and trying to get the win. That is the stuff of dreams for a spinner."  The victory also keeps alive South Africa's hopes of defending their World Test Championship title next year having beaten Australia at Lord's in the previous decider in 2025.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Power bills and data centers cast rare spotlight on utilities in US midterms
item.description: NEW YORK, Oct 31 : US electricity prices had flown under the radar in past national elections, but they have become a major political issue in this year's midterms as Americans grow angry over rising utility bills and deals for power-hungry data centers.Nationwide, according to Energy Information Administrati

FAST

NEW YORK, Oct 31 : US electricity prices had flown under the radar in past national elections, but they have become a major political issue in this year's midterms as Americans grow angry over rising utility bills and deals for power-hungry data centers. Nationwide, according to Energy Information Administration data, electricity prices for homes have risen more than 10 per cent since 2024 when President Donald Trump was elected along with Republican majorities in both houses of the US Congress. Higher electricity prices have outpaced the rise in costs for other goods and services. Power bills have grown even faster in political battleground states of Ohio, Michigan and Pennsylvania, which are also hot spots for new data centers. In some cases, electricity bills have soared by triple the inflation rate.  Many politicians vying for top statehouse seats across the country this year have backed cracking down on utilities. Some have proposed freezing utility rate increases and slashing guaranteed returns, steps that could have sweeping consequences for the country's utility industry.

"It could be the first election to feature utilities and electricity, specifically, as a prominent issue in the midterms," said Charles Hua, executive director of PowerLines, a nonprofit that advocates reforming utility policy to favor consumers. "Part of that is because people's utility bills have gone up and up, and they don't see any end in sight."  Utilities are heavily regulated. State regulators generally must approve utilities’ requests to spend on the grid and to recover those costs through rate increases. Regulators also set the return on equity utilities can earn on their grid investments.  This year, utilities are on track to match last year's record high $31 billion in rate increase requests to regulators, a PowerLines survey showed.  Last year's spending was double the previous record. The investor-owned companies are also expected to carry out a record of nearly $1.3 trillion in capital spending over the next five years, according to an analysis by S&P Global’s Regulatory Research Associates. UTILITIES SPOTLIGHTED Seats on nine state public utility commissions are up for election this year, nearly all the US states where voters elect their utility regulators. These include burgeoning data center hubs Arizona and Georgia. Governors will be chosen in 36 US states this year, and governors appoint utility regulators in states where commissioners are not directly elected.  In Ohio, Democrat Amy Acton has promised to lower energy bills if she is elected governor. Her campaign said she will also appoint a public utilities commission that was "not beholden to utility companies" and work with the state attorney general to crack down on "excessive rate hikes and predatory practices." Ohio's residential electricity bills have grown by more than 20 per cent over the last two years, according to EIA data. Acton has also said she supports a data center moratorium. Her Republican opponent Vivek Ramaswamy said he would assure Ohioans living near data centers would not pay electricity bills at all. BULLY PULPIT Some governors who are up for reelection have used their political weight to pressure the power industry to keep prices down. In April, Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro announced that prominent utility, PECO Energy Company, had acceded to his demand that it withdraw its proposal with state regulators to increase rates. Shapiro, a Democrat running for reelection, said the move would reduce future utility bills by as much as $34 a month. He followed up with a letter to more utility CEOs seeking changes in how utilities justify spending and returns on equity. "The governors are using this crisis on energy affordability as an opportunity to take a deeper dive into the utility regulatory model and see if it makes any sense," said Jamie Van Nostrand, senior fellow at the Kleinman Center for Energy Policy at the University of Pennsylvania and former chair of the Massachusetts Department of Public Utilities.  Power bills tracked low inflation for roughly a decade, and were not an issue in most mainstream elections until last year, when Mikie Sherrill successfully ran for New Jersey governor on the promise of freezing utility bills. She did so the same day she took office. In Virginia, home to the largest concentration of data centers in the world, Governor Abigail Spanberger took a similar approach, which industry analysts said could offer a playbook for those who win this year’s elections.  Utility advocates say reducing guaranteed returns and freezing rates will not make a meaningful difference in household bills but could lead to a long-term reduction of investments in the grid. "The grid is America's greatest machine, and it doesn't operate on the political calendar,” said Drew Maloney, president of Edison Electric Institute, a trade organization for investor-owned electric utilities. “It requires consistent investment every year to deliver reliable energy to our customers." Credit rating agency Fitch downgraded the North American utility sector to "deteriorating" from "neutral" in June, citing political pressure in the midterms to limit electricity bills and utility profits. For an industry that plans in decades, it is hard to predict the result of short-term political moves aimed at saving money for households. "I do think the real meat will come after the election," Hua said.

Source: Reuters

Residents of Russian-controlled Ukrainian town arrive in Belarus

Hundreds of starving and exhausted residents left the town of Oleshky on Friday during a US-backed local ceasefire, the first of its kind and the longest humanitarian pause in the war, which is nearing its fifth year.

People attend an evacuation from the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, amid Russia's attack on Ukraine, in the Kherson region, in this handout picture released Oct 30, 2026. Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine, Kyrylo Budanov/Handout via Reuters

KYIV: Four planes carrying residents evacuated from the Russian-controlled Ukrainian town of Oleshky landed in Belarus on Saturday (Oct 31), the Belarusian Belta state news agency and a senior Ukrainian official said. Hundreds of starving and exhausted residents left the town of Oleshky on Friday during a US-backed local ceasefire, the first of its kind and the longest humanitarian pause in the war, which is nearing its fifth year. "The last, fourth plane landed in Gomel," said David Arakhamia, a top Ukrainian peace negotiator and close ally of President Volodymyr Zelenskiy. "In a few hours, all Ukrainian citizens evacuated from Oleshky together with a Ukrainian delegation will be on Ukrainian territory."

Belta later reported that a convoy of buses carrying the residents had departed from the airport in Gomel, in southeastern Belarus near the border with Ukraine. The evacuees leaving for Ukraine had to take a complicated route to leave Oleshky as the frontline runs just a few kilometres away. They first travelled by bus via Crimea to the Russian town of Anapa before flying to Belarus from where they will continue to Ukraine via a border crossing, Belta said. The local ceasefire in Oleshky was reached thanks to mediation efforts by US first lady Melania Trump and with the pope's involvement. The ceasefire has been holding since Tuesday without violations, according to both Ukrainian and Russian officials. It has allowed them to de-mine the roads and bring food, medicines and other supplies into the town. Supply routes to Oleshky were disrupted by fighting and drones. According to some residents, food deliveries were stopped in May, pushing hundreds of people into starvation. It was not immediately clear how many people decided to leave Oleshky and how many opted to stay in the town. Oleshky residents had options to travel to Russia or to return to Ukraine. Ukrainian officials have said around 1,700 people remained in Oleshky from a pre-war population of about 24,000. According to several residents interviewed by Reuters, many of those were elderly or ill.

Source: Reuters/kl

French presidential candidate Mélenchon joins protest in Paris Jean-Luc Mélenchon, the France Unbowed (La France Insoumise) candidate for the 2027 French presidential election, on Saturday participated in the demonstration as the protest against the rising cost of living in the country enters its third weekend, according to France24. ANI | Updated: 31-10-2026 21:02 IST | Created: 31-10-2026 21:02 IST

France Unbowed leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon joins nationwide protests (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Jean-Luc Mélenchon, the France Unbowed (La France Insoumise) candidate for the 2027 French presidential election, on Saturday participated in the demonstration as the protest against the rising cost of living in the country enters its third weekend, according to France24. The left-wing leader Mélenchon had also joined the protests on October 24, last weekend. According to the French media outlet, about 15,000 people joined the demonstrations today, while the Interior Ministry noted that the events unfolded "without any notable incidents”. Police have made 27 arrests by 2:00 pm (local time), in contrast to 217 arrests a week ago. The country witnessed heightened security as protests coincided with Halloween, deploying around 70,000 security personnel amid fears that demonstrators could use festive masks to conceal their identities. French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez had warned of a "very high risk" of unrest, assuring that authorities would respond firmly to any violence. "Everyone is on deck to ensure an extremely firm response to any trouble," Nunez said at a news conference earlier this week, outlining security arrangements for Saturday. France24 reported that the transportation authorities closed several metro and suburban stations in the Paris metropolitan area, with more than 40 stations affected. The demonstrations in France gained momentum in late September as President Emmanuel Macron's minority government began discussions on the 2027 budget. With public debt approaching 120 per cent of economic output and borrowing costs rising, the government faces mounting pressure to reduce spending. Students protesting the deteriorating condition of schools, overcrowded classrooms and an admissions system widely perceived as unfair have been joined by trade unions and members of the resurgent 'Yellow Vest' movement, which is demanding action on the cost of living. Meanwhile in Germany today, the protesters took to the streets under the banner of campaign group "Gen Z regelt" (Gen Z takes charge). As per France24, the protesters oppose compulsory military service and demand more investment in education amid inflation. Currently, there is a wider wave of youth-led demonstrations across Europe, with protesters raising concerns over the cost of living, declining educational facilities, social inequality and diminishing economic prospects. (ANI)

When buses stopped running on Brazil election day, ‘Lula’s Army’ grabbed their car keys

Reuters

31 October, 2026 02:00 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

By Luciana Magalhaes and Lisandra Paraguassu SALVADOR, Brazil, Oct 31 (Reuters) – When buses in the northeastern Brazilian city of Salvador inexplicably stopped running last Sunday, history teacher Martins Mafra grabbed his car keys and set off to pick up stranded voters across town.

Mafra’s efforts in Salvador, the capital of Bahia state, were part of a massive get-out-the-vote drive across Brazil that helped power leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva to an unprecedented fourth term.

Lula supporters, shocked by right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro’s first-round lead, quickly mobilized as the prospect sank in that the Bolsonaro clan could return to power. They used innovative social media initiatives, free taxi rides and grassroots campaigning to secure the incumbent president over 10 million more votes in the runoff.

Show Full Article

“I’m a father, and I work in education, so this was an opportunity to teach and show that we can make a difference,” said Mafra, who offered rides to supporters of all stripes. “It’s one thing to stay home complaining about city hall or posting videos online; it’s another thing to get up, walk out the door, and actually do something.”

Bolsonaro, son of jailed former President Jair Bolsonaro, fled this week to the US, where he declared himself the legitimate “leader” of Brazil, questioning the credibility of Lula’s 10 million-vote leap.

Bolsonaro also questioned a two-hour voting extension, requested by Lula’s campaign and granted by a Lula-appointed Supreme Court justice, due to the out-of-service buses in Bahia. Bolsonaro’s campaign also sought an extension due to rains in conservative-leaning southern states, and the extension had little bearing on the result, the federal electoral court said.

LULA STRONGHOLD

Bahia, a populous Lula stronghold, was the state with the highest fall in abstention rates between both rounds, with nearly 400,000 more people voting in the runoff.

Almost a quarter of those additional voters came from Salvador, a city of over 2.5 million people where Lula won 73% of runoff votes.

Salvador resident Gabriel Mercury, 41, son of Brazilian pop star Daniela Mercury, was one of those who helped orchestrate the turnaround.

The Lula voter watched with concern as the leftist underperformed in the first round, and decided to do something about it. He began by inviting undecided voters to have coffee with him and talk politics. Later, he offered cash rewards of up to 2,400 reais ($445.67) to anyone who could name a single Bolsonaro legislative proposal that had benefited workers.

Nobody took him up on the offer.

LULA OVERHAULS CAMPAIGN

After the underwhelming first round, Lula’s team sought to reboot a campaign marred by infighting, mixed messaging and the complacency of incumbency, aides said.

Aware that no presidential candidate had ever been elected after trailing in the initial vote, the 81-year-old Lula bought his first ever smartphone to reach Brazilians on the platforms that increasingly shape Brazil’s political debate.

Meanwhile, lawmaker Andre Janones, who helped Lula beat Jair Bolsonaro in 2022, rapidly expanded a WhatsApp channel he called “Lula’s Army.”

By instructing followers to recruit friends and amplify Lula content online, he grew the channel from roughly 50,000 people ahead of the first round to over 10 million by the runoff.

Dharma political risk consultant Creomar de Souza said Lula’s team, and particularly Janones, successfully pounced on missteps by Bolsonaro to convince voters he would threaten Brazil’s democracy, reverse social advances and slash welfare payments on which millions of Brazilians depend.

As the runoff approached, polls showed Lula closing the gap on Bolsonaro. By election day, they were tied.

In Salvador, Mercury began to believe Lula could win. Then, early on Sunday, Salvador’s bus network ground to a halt.

BUS FIASCO

In Brazil, public authorities are required to provide free public transport on election day.

But reports from across Salvador, where Mayor Bruno Reis supported Bolsonaro, suggested many buses were not running.

Inspectors from the Bahia consumer protection agency found 944 buses idling in Salvador depots. Jaime Barreiros Neto, the Bahia electoral court’s judicial analyst, estimated at least 30% of the fleet was not operating.

Reis blamed the outage on Lula stickers that had been placed on buses in violation of electoral rules. As soon as city hall realized sticker removal efforts were causing a bottleneck, it immediately ordered the fleet released, he said in a press conference on Sunday.

Reis told Reuters he supported Bolsonaro in the runoff in accordance with his party, União Brasil. He denied detaining public transport or hindering voter mobility, saying the stickering of the buses held up the fleet.

Bahia’s electoral court ordered the arrest of Salvador’s transportation chief, Pablo Souza, over the absent buses. It revoked the order once voting had ended the following day, but demanded a probe into the incident.

Souza, who was in Paris on an official visit during the day of the vote, denied wrongdoing. He told Reuters the number of buses was the same as during the first round, and in line with electoral regulations.

MASS MOBILIZATIONS

As news of idling buses rippled through Salvador, Mercury and five friends asked their social media followers to drive people to voting stations. Some people got behind the wheel; others donated to cover fuel costs. Mercury estimated that his team moved around 600 voters on election day.

“Politics isn’t just institutional politics,” he said. “We make politics through our actions.”

Uber drivers also stepped up, with thousands offering free rides worth up to 50 reais ($9.28) throughout the day, said Adriano de Jesus Braga dos Santos, an Uber driver and content creator, who personally offered 36 rides to passengers.

Nicole Soares, 18, waited 40 minutes for a bus, but never considered giving up. “I had the right to vote,” she said, casting her ballot for Lula.

Some residents were still unable to vote.

Grecia de Jesus Nunes, a 54-year-old street vendor, said only two buses passed her hotdog stand between 8 a.m. and 2 p.m. No buses were available during her brief break, and when volunteer drivers eventually reached her, she could no longer leave work.

Though unable to vote, Nunes rejoiced at Lula’s victory.

“My life is Lula,” she said. “I am Lula until I die.”

($1 = 5.3851 reais)

(Reporting by Luciana Magalhaes, Editing by Gabriel Stargardter and David Gregorio)

FAST

RAWALPINDI: Pakistan’s military is “cautiously optimistic” about its mediation between Iran and the United States, its spokesman said on Friday (Oct 30) in his first interview since a high-level delegation visited Tehran this week. Army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir - Pakistan's chief mediator in its efforts to de-escalate the now eight-month-old Iran war - has been to Tehran twice this month, most recently on Monday alongside Saudi and Turkish officials. “Why would the Field Marshal be going twice if it is not for some positivity? So yes, of course,” spokesman Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said when asked whether the trips were a positive sign. “The word that we would use is always cautiously optimistic,” added Chaudhry, director general of Inter-Services Public Relations.

There were still "powerful spoilers and detractors" who believed conflict serves them, he added without naming them. Speaking in the garrison city of Rawalpindi, where Pakistan's armed forces are headquartered, Chaudhry declined to say what was discussed or whether the United States had backed the trip. Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin joined Munir in Tehran on Monday. Their two countries signed a joint defence pact with Pakistan on Aug 7, saying an attack on any signatory will be treated as an attack on all. The Mecca Joint Defence Agreement has taken on added significance as the Iran war has redrawn regional alliances and raised fears of a broader Middle East conflict. While the three signatories say the agreement is aimed at collective deterrence and regional security, analysts see its evolution as closely tied to efforts by regional powers to manage the fallout from the Iran-US confrontation. After Monday’s talks, Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, said regional security should be ensured by regional countries without foreign intervention. The wording of the pact does not bar new members, Chaudhry said on Friday when asked whether Iran could join. “Anyone who has a shared vision of collective deterrence and regional peace, why not? Everyone is most welcome,” he said, adding that it was for the political leadership of the three principal parties to decide. Asked whether more Pakistani troops were being sent to Saudi Arabia under the agreement, Chaudhry said that would depend on the situation and the decision of both countries’ political leadership. He said Pakistan was committed to defending Saudi Arabia and the holy sites of Mecca and Medina. "We are not part of the Yemeni conflict, which is an intra-Yemen conflict," he added. Fighting between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi group has been reignited by the Iran conflict, stoking fears of a wider war. HOME FRONT On the home front, the federal government suspended the provincial government in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, led by jailed former prime minister Imran Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), on Oct 11 and detained Chief Minister Sohail Afridi. The government had accused the provincial administration of failing to tackle militancy. The PTI rejected the allegations and says its government took part in counter-terrorism efforts. PTI leaders called the move a pretext to crush protests. Asked if there would now be larger military-led campaigns in the province, Chaudhry said that was not how the army conducted counter-terrorism. "Our counter-terrorism operations are based on what we call IBOs, intelligence-based operations ... The tempo of the freedom of action of (those) IBOs will further increase," he said. Independents backed by Khan’s PTI won the most directly elected seats in the February 2024 election but fell short of a majority. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa was the only province controlled by Khan’s party. Khan has been in jail since 2023, and his supporters see the military behind his imprisonment and the dismantlement of the PTI. The army denies involvement in politics.

FAST

SEPANG, Malaysia, Oct 31 : KTM's Pedro Acosta won a thrilling Malaysian Grand Prix sprint at the Sepang International Circuit on Saturday, while Ducati's Marc Marquez finished second, capitalising on MotoGP title rival Jorge Martin's withdrawal. Gresini Racing's pole sitter Alex Marquez crashed out of the lead on lap three, while Trackhouse rider Ai Ogura, who led for most of the 10-lap sprint, conceded positions towards the end to finish fourth, behind Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi. Rain had threatened to play spoilsport in Sepang but the leading pack crossed the finish line of the 10-lap sprint just before the heavens opened up. "Normally in mixed conditions I don't do a good job. But anyway, today was the day to try," Acosta said after his second sprint victory of the season.

"I was playing for nothing. Also knowing that Marc was behind fighting for the championship ... It was my opportunity to try to make something different from this." Martin withdrew after persistent wrist pain hampered his comeback from a fracture, with the Spaniard acknowledging that his title hopes were "already lost". The sprint podium extended reigning champion Marc's lead over Martin to 19 points, with the Ducati rider set to increase his advantage further in Sunday's race. 'I DIDN'T WANT TO LEAD' Marc said he was happy to finish second, avoiding any risks in treacherous conditions in some parts of the circuit. "The guys that are not fighting for the championship can take more risk. I was calm," Marc said. "I had the pace, but I didn't want to lead the race because the one that arrives first is the one that normally crashes." Alex had snatched pole position from his brother, and the Gresini Racing rider stormed into the lead at turn one, while Marc fell to fourth when he was overtaken by an aggressive Ogura, who forced Acosta to take evasive action. But dark clouds loomed over the circuit while spots of rain appeared at the track and Alex — who won the race here last year — crashed out of the lead on lap three at turn 13, giving Ogura the lead. Prima Pramac's Jack Miller gambled on an early pit stop, but the Australian was left furious after his team failed to have his spare Yamaha bike fitted with wet tyres in time. BIKE SWAP GAMBLE Only the backmarkers rolled the dice on a bike swap while the leaders stayed out, convinced that the rapidly drying track did not justify a switch to wet tyres. Ogura and Acosta traded places with three laps remaining, but the Japanese rider came off worse in the exchange, leaving the door open for Marc to overtake and move into second while Bezzecchi also climbed to third. "I knew I could manage well to have something for the end, and then the rain came, so it was a little bit unexpected and I saw the others were struggling a bit," said Bezzecchi, who is 52 points behind Marc in third. "Step by step, I was catching (up) and I was closer. Unfortunately, I didn't catch them early enough to try to battle with Marc."

item.content:encoded:
Iran claims US struck fishing boats off Qeshm Island, two injured As reported by the news agency IRNA, the two fishermen who went missing after the drone attack have been found, according to the CEO of the Qeshm Fishing Community. Both were sent back to Qeshm Island. ANI | Updated: 31-10-2026 18:39 IST | Created: 31-10-2026 18:39 IST

Representative image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

Country:

Iran

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The United States reportedly struck two fishing boats off Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, injuring two Iranian fishermen. As reported by the news agency IRNA, the two fishermen who went missing after the drone attack have been found, according to the CEO of the Qeshm Fishing Community. Both were sent back to Qeshm Island. Meanwhile, one of the two injured fishermen was taken to a hospital, Al Jazeera reported, citing Fars news agency. “This incident occurred around 11:30 am today involving two fishing boats within 18 miles of the village of Musan, affiliated with Qeshm County… Each boat had two occupants,” the deputy governor of Hormozgan Province for political, security, and social affairs told Tasnim news agency, as per Al Jazeera. As strikes continue in the Strait of Hormuz, earlier, Iranian naval forces destroyed an "enemy submarine" and damaged two commercial oil tankers in the operational zone east of Hormuz on Friday morning. State media Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting (IRIB) reported, citing the Iranian Navy's Public Relations department, that Iranian forces targeted and destroyed an adversary submarine navigating the operational sector near the vital maritime choke point. "This morning, an enemy submarine that was operating in the operational area east of the Strait of Hormuz was hit and destroyed by Iranian Navy sailors," the Navy statement read. Meanwhile, the Commander of the United States Central Command (CENTCOM), Admiral Brad Cooper, on Friday (local time) stated that the primary internationally recognised transit routes in the Strait of Hormuz have been successfully cleared of Iranian sea mines and commercial vessels are sailing freely through the strategic waterway. "Earlier this week, I visited some of the more than 50,000 service members supporting operations across the Middle East, including our mission in the Strait of Hormuz. When I flew over the strait, I saw dozens of commercial vessels transiting—all types: cargo, crude oil, liquid natural gas, or LNG. And I also saw our U.S. assets in the air and on the water, including a squadron of advanced sea drones that were on patrol, supporting a defensive layer," Admiral Cooper stated. This comes as the possibility of fresh strikes lurks in Iran. Today, Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei ordered senior commanders to confront all the threats “with an immediate, effective, and unrestricted geographical response.” According to a series of X posts by the account of Mojtaba Khamenei, the Iranian leader met with senior commanders of the armed forces against the backdrop of possibilities of fresh escalation between the United States and Iran. “Every level and type of threat must be confronted with an immediate, effective, and unrestricted geographical response,” the statement read. (ANI)

(This story has not been edited by Devdiscourse staff and is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

Hong Kong telecom company agrees to halt US operations under pressure

The Federal Communications Commission has previously barred China Mobile, China Telecom and China Unicom from providing international telecommunications services to the United States, citing broad national security concerns.

FAST

WASHINGTON: HKT, a leading Hong Kong telecom carrier and subsidiary of PCCW Ltd, on Friday (Oct 30) agreed to halt its operations in the United States under pressure from the Federal Communications Commission. The FCC in October 2025 said it was moving to revoke the authority of HKT to operate in the United States, citing national security concerns and its affiliation with China Unicom, which is a shareholder in PCCW. Under a consent decree reviewed by Reuters, HKT has agreed to stop international and domestic telecom services to and within the United States. HKT must file an application with the FCC within 30 days to discontinue services and must discontinue US services by September 1, 2027. PCCW declined immediate comment. The agreement means the FCC will not move forward with the revocation proceeding that could have offered more details on Washington's national security concerns.
